title: Grade 2 Social Studies — Comparing Types of Communities
subject: Social Studies
description: Practice with questions on urban, suburban, rural, neighborhoods.
creator: Teach Arcade

questions.question: Which place is most likely part of an urban area?
choices: a dirt trail across a remote ranch

questions.question: Which place is most likely rural?
choices: a row of offices beside a subway
a farming area with homes far apart

questions.question: What often describes a suburban community?
choices: homes near a city, outside its busiest center
a mountain with no roads or houses
a farm alone on a distant plain

questions.question: Which need can people have in urban, suburban, and rural communities?
choices: wide farm fields on every block
tall office towers beside each home

questions.question: Which detail most suggests a city center?
Which could a rural community have?
choices: a school serving families from farms and small towns
a rule against all public buildings
a building tall enough to touch the Moon
no places for people to meet

questions.question: Why might a small town share a library with nearby towns?
choices: to serve more people using resources together
to make it harder to get books
to move all homes into the library

questions.question: What can a community map help you compare?
choices: how near homes are to a park
what each person had for lunch

questions.question: Which example shows communities working together?
choices: Two towns get different amounts of snow.
Roads are longer in one town.
Each town puts signs in a different color.
Towns share a place to recycle materials.

questions.question: A shop stands near homes, a school, and a small park. What do these places help make?
What word names a group of people who live in or share a place?
Why might a city have more public bus stops close together than an area with widely spaced homes?
choices: Many people live or travel within a small area.

questions.question: What can be shared by families in very different communities?
A map shows several houses close to a large city but outside its center. Which term may fit?
Why might some families in a less crowded area travel farther to reach shops?
choices: The roads always turn away from shops.
Buildings may be spread farther apart.
All shops are open only at night.

questions.question: Which is a way residents can help their community?
Which detail would best help compare how crowded two areas are?
choices: the color of each town's flag
how many people live in the same size of area
the name of the largest street

questions.question: Which setting has homes and people closest together?
choices: a wide wildlife area with one cabin

questions.question: How might a town learn where a new playground is needed?
choices: ask families and map existing playgrounds
pick the site farthest from all homes
ask nobody and erase old maps

questions.question: What can change when a community grows?
choices: it may need more places for people to live
everyone must have the same job
